punch_items.evidence: Done-when ('point-to-point, ladder, and mesh builders all emit the same network type') demonstrated: tests/test_builders.py::test_all_builders_emit_resistor_network asserts all three builders return pathminer.core.network.ResistorNetwork, and test_all_builders_produce_solvable_networks asserts each solves to a TwoTerminalResult. 65 targeted tests pass.

ResistorNetwork.edge_list() produces the backend-neutral [(u,v,r)] the Session 04 dispatcher consumes, and ResistorNetwork.two_terminal() delegates to two_terminal_resistance; backend passthrough agreement tested (tests/test_network.py::test_backend_passthrough_agrees, test_network_matches_raw_solver). Whole-item closure remains with the dispatcher owner; left open.

pathminer/analysis/model_selection.py selects point_to_point/ladder/mesh from geometry with a stated reason and escalates or warns on square/complex/unknown pours instead of silently laddering; user override honoured with marker and retained warning. Covered by tests/test_model_selection.py. UI reason/override wiring is a later session; left open.

Fast-vs-mesh correlation and mesh-refinement convergence fixtures: tests/test_builders.py::test_fast_ladder_matches_mesh_within_tolerance (mesh within 3% of the ladder on a strip-like pour) and test_mesh_converges_toward_ladder_as_pitch_refines (monotone convergence to <1% as pitch refines). Full cost/backend-choice closure is a later session; left open.

apis_changed: pathminer.core.network: NEW Node, Provenance, Edge, TwoTerminalResult, ResistorNetwork (add_edge, merge, canonical, edge_list, two_terminal, from_edges, nodes, node_count, edge_count, notes, terminals)

pathminer.analysis.builders: NEW build_point_to_point, TraceSegment, ViaSegment, Segment, build_ladder, LADDER_MIN_ASPECT, build_mesh, DEFAULT_MESH_PITCH_MM, PourGeometry, pour_geometry, ViaStation, Tie
pathminer.analysis.model_selection: NEW MODELS, ModelChoice, select_model, select_model_for_pour
compatibility_consequences: Additive only: no existing API signature, schema, default, unit, tolerance, or numerical behavior changed.
pathminer/core/__init__.py and pathminer/analysis/__init__.py were not modified (out of scope); new modules are imported by full dotted path. Session 08 may re-export them through the package hubs.
decisions: Equipotential ties modelled as union-find node merges (ResistorNetwork.merge + edge_list collapse), not near-zero tie resistors, preserving v0.13's solver-conditioning contract.
The solver's shared _prepare stays the single resistance validator; add_edge does not re-validate, so build->solve raises the same named errors as a raw edge list.

Pure builders take explicit geometry/topology inputs (ViaStation, Tie, a .net/.fills pour), not a BoardSource; BoardSource wiring is a later integration/PWR session, matching where that orchestration lived in v0.13 build_graph_pour.

Model-selection escalates to the mesh when pour aspect < LADDER_MIN_ASPECT (v0.13's 2:1), when flagged complex, or when geometry is unknown; strip-like pours use the ladder; overrides retain a marker and any warning (S8.7).
assumptions: geo passed to builders is the per-copper-layer mapping shape from Stackup.geometry() (name, z_top_mm, finished_mm, z_ctr_mm) that pathminer.core.resistance expects.
A pour is represented as .net + .fills ({layer: [(x, y), ...]}), matching pathminer.models.board.Pour.
deviations: Mesh determinism refinement (numerics-preserving): v0.13's mesh_pour_edges picked a via hub cell and a tie's nearest cell by set iteration order; build_mesh iterates live cells sorted and breaks nearest-cell ties by cell index. All cells a barrel covers merge to one node regardless, so the two-terminal result is unchanged; only node identity becomes reproducible (test_mesh_is_deterministic).

build_ladder does not itself skip a vialess pour; v0.13 made that decision in build_graph_pour orchestration. The strip/rung/tie numerics are identical for the overlapping case; the 'ignore a vialess pour' policy belongs to the caller.
known_issues: Builders are not yet wired to a BoardSource; track-vs-pour clipping, pad-in-pour tie discovery, and via-array clustering (v0.13 build_graph_pour) are the integration layer's job and out of scope.
No routed net-graph builder ('routed traces/vias without zones') is provided; select_model names that case as point_to_point.

Fast-vs-mesh agreement depends on matching boundary conditions; a single point tie legitimately shows a larger mesh-vs-ladder gap (physical constriction resistance the 1-D ladder cannot represent), which is why the QA-005 fixture distributes the end injection across the pour width.
dependent_session_impact: Session 08 (compatibility integration / single-file build) may re-export ResistorNetwork and the builders through the untouched package hubs.
Session 13 (headless runner / factorization reuse, ARCH-007): ResistorNetwork.edge_list() is the stable point to build/factor a graph once per net/model and back-solve pairs.

PWR sessions: model_selection.select_model_for_pour and the three builders are the entry points for the routed/pour analysis runner; ModelChoice carries the reason/override/warnings the result renderer needs.
recommended_next_action: Coordinator review of the diff and handoff; on approval, integrate at the recorded final commit and open dependent sessions (08, 13, and the PWR wave). Optionally assign the paired ChatGPT prompt as a read-only reviewer of the numerics.
